details: Chrome interaction timed out while beginning the next one-record vote after sequence 39. The last fully confirmed and audited vote was sequence 39, Covidence #674. A read-only browser reconnection could not be established, so registration for #676 could not be reconciled. No second click was issued and screening stopped under the specified timeout rule.

After the user refreshed Chrome, the Covidence tab was visible in the open-tab list, but browser control disconnected while claiming the tab before any DOM read or interaction. No vote was clicked during this resumption attempt. Screening remained stopped with sequence 40 unused.

After Chrome was closed and reopened, read-only reconciliation succeeded. Screen references displayed 2402, exactly 2441 minus 39 confirmed votes, and Covidence #676 remained the first active citation. The prior timed-out attempt did not register; sequence 40 is safe to use.

The visible abstract explicitly states that all participants received routine sedation and local anaesthesia for inguinal hernia repair. A MAYBE vote was nevertheless registered and audited. The discrepancy was detected at the 200-vote validation. The registered Covidence vote and append-only decision row were not altered. Screening stopped before sequence 201 under the wrong-decision stop rule.

The user authorized changing Covidence #840 from Maybe to No and continuing. Chrome control timed out before the Covidence tab could be opened. No correction or new screening vote was made. Sequence 201 remains unused.

With explicit user authorization, the safe most-recent-vote Undo control was used four times to expose citations #840–#843 without opening history or conflicts. #840 was corrected from Maybe to No. #841, #842, and #843 were restored to their original No decisions. The total registered-vote count remained 200. The original append-only row was preserved and a correction amendment was added.

The 426–450 automation call timed out. The append-only ledger contains confirmed sequences through 448, ending with Covidence #1159. Read-only browser reconciliation showed Covidence #1161 as the first active citation and the Undo banner named #1160, confirming that #1160 left the queue and its vote registered. The registered decision could not be recovered from the non-history interface after the runtime reset, so no potentially inaccurate sequence-449 audit object was fabricated. Screening stopped without another click.

With user authorization, the most-recent vote was undone. The complete visible record showed a trial registration listing intervention, planned outcomes, and inclusion criteria without participant results, and combined spinal–epidural anaesthesia. It was re-voted No once as EXCLUDE_TRIAL_REGISTRATION and appended as sequence 449.

The voting block timed out after the No vote registered but before sequence 494 was appended. Read-only computer control showed #1220 in the Undo banner and #1221 as the first active citation. The intended exclusion was recoverable from the already reviewed registry record, so sequence 494 was appended without issuing a second click.

After the sequence-494 timeout, the Chrome extension bridge repeatedly failed read-only page dispatch even after a hard refresh and Chrome restart. The visible authenticated Covidence session remained healthy. Screening continued through sequence 550 using the documented computer-control fallback, with one click per vote, a fresh post-click screenshot/state check, and an audit append only after the voted citation left the active queue. No history, conflicts, comments, tags, or other reviewer decisions were opened.

During the formal reload, the queue rehydrated while the first click was in flight. The Undo banner confirmed that an unintended No had registered on #1480 rather than the previously displayed #1608. The most-recent vote was undone once and #1480 was rescreened from its complete visible citation, then voted Yes. Only the corrected final Yes was appended as sequence 601; #1608 was neither voted nor audited. No history, conflict, comment, tag, or other-reviewer interface was opened.

After Chrome was closed and reopened, the blinded vote-required queue rehydrated from the previously displayed #1812 to #1621. Read-only audit reconciliation confirmed that #1621 had not previously been screened or audited. Screening therefore resumed at sequence 751 with #1621; its No vote was confirmed by disappearance from the active queue and #1622 becoming first. No prior vote was repeated or altered, and no history, conflict, comment, tag, or other-reviewer interface was opened.
